core_obligations: Set A = O_{X,x} and B = O_{Y,y}; use the criterion for geometric reducedness at a point to see that A is geometrically reduced, hence B is a localization of A tensor_k K (proof lines 8488-8491).

Take A -> A' as in the pre-delta construction and form B' = B tensor over (A tensor_k K) with (A' tensor_k K); show B' is finite over B and that B -> B' induces an isomorphism on total rings of fractions, by choosing f in m_A satisfying the equivalent conditions and observing that the same f plays the same role for B because dim(B) = 1 and A_f = A'_f (proof lines 8492-8501).
Let B'' be the integral closure of B in its total ring of fractions, so that B' is contained in B'' and the delta-invariant of Y at y equals length_B(B''/B) (proof lines 8502-8505).
Complete the comparison by the displayed chain of length inequalities, obtaining the asserted inequality between the two delta-invariants (proof lines 8506-8520).
proof_roadmap: Identify the base-changed local ring as a localization of the tensor product.
Transport the pre-delta construction across the field extension.
Compare with the integral closure and express both delta-invariants as lengths.
Conclude the inequality by the length comparison.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the inequality delta(X at x) <= delta(Y at y) for the base change Y = X_K, under geometric reducedness of X at x and the dimension-one assumption on both local rings. The proof sets A and B equal to the two local rings, uses geometric reducedness of A to identify B as a localization of A tensor_k K, and then compares the two delta-invariants through the intermediate ring A' of the pre-delta construction and its base change B' = B tensor (A' tensor_k K), which is finite over B with the same total ring of fractions (proof lines 8488-8503). Writing B'' for the integral closure of B in its total ring of fractions and using B' contained in B'', the delta-invariant of Y at y is length_B(B''/B), and the proof compares this length with length_B(B'/B) and continues the chain of inequalities (proof lines 8504-8520). H2: the identification of the base-changed intermediate ring and the length comparison are the substance.
